The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide for launching a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that is configured with an NVIDIA RTX A6000‑style GPU (note that Google Cloud currently offers the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** as the closest high‑end GPU; the RTX A6000 itself is not listed in the public GPU catalog). The instance will run **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | How to set up |
|------|---------------|
| **Google Cloud SDK** (`gcloud`) | Install from <https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install> |
| **Project ID** | Create or select a project in the Cloud Console |
| **Billing enabled** | Ensure billing is attached to the project |
| **API enabled** | Enable the *Compute Engine API* (via Cloud Console or `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`) |
| **Permissions** | You need `roles/compute.admin` (or equivalent) on the project |

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Explanation of key flags

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1` | Adds one NVIDIA Tesla A100 GPU. Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with another GPU type if you want a different model. |
| `--boot-disk-size=200GB` | Size of the boot disk (SSD). Adjust based on your workload. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` | Optional: runs a shell script at first boot (e.g., to install CUDA, drivers). |
| `--tags=http-server,https-server` | Opens ports 80/443 in the firewall. |

> **Tip:** If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to check whether Google Cloud has added it to their GPU catalog. As of now, the **Tesla A100** is the closest match in terms of performance.

---

## 3. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s a minimal request body you can POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-4"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values.  
Send the request with an OAuth 2.0 access token that has the `compute.instances.create` scope.

---

## 4. After Creation

Once the instance is running:

1. **SSH into the VM** (via Cloud Console or `gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a`).
2. **Verify GPU availability**:

   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```

3. **Install CUDA / cuDNN** if you plan to run GPU workloads. The startup script above installs CUDA 11.4; adjust as needed.

---

## 5. Cleaning Up

To avoid incurring charges, delete the instance when you’re done:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete rtx-a6000-demo --zone us-central1-a
```

---

### Quick Reference

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `gcloud compute instances create ...` | Creates the VM via CLI |
| `gcloud compute instances delete ...` | Deletes the VM |
| `gcloud compute instances list` | Lists all VMs in the project |
| `gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-demo` | Shows detailed config |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, GPU count, or disk size to fit your specific workload. Happy computing!
